easy_fields.name: MATHVISTA
easy_fields.creator: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao
easy_fields.description: MATHVISTA is a benchmark designed to combine challenges from diverse mathematical and visual tasks. It consists of 6,141 examples, derived from 28 existing multimodal datasets and 3 newly created datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, and PaperQA). Completing these tasks requires fine-grained, deep visual understanding and compositional reasoning, which all state-of-the-art foundation models find challenging.

G3_collection.reasoning: The paper extensively details the data collection process, including sources (28 existing, 3 new datasets), selection criteria (heuristic rules, expert annotators), and balancing representation.

G4_annotation.reasoning: The paper describes manual annotation by graduate students, a two-step review process, inter-annotator consistency rates (99.2% and Fleiss Kappa 0.775), and annotator demographics (high school diploma or higher).

G5_rai.reasoning: The paper includes a dedicated 'Limitations of the Benchmark' section discussing dataset coverage and annotation consistency, and examples in the 'Natural Image' section touch upon sensitive information (age gap) and model restrictions related to images of people.

G6_processing.reasoning: The paper details data preparation steps, including splitting into testmini and test sets, sampling strategy, quality checks, and a commitment to maintaining the datasets and an online evaluation platform.
